GainsBlock.rationale: `public override bool GainsBlock => true` (SecondWind.cs:15) == the class attribute.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (SecondWind.cs:21-24) == cost 1 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF. Second Wind has no Exhaust keyword of its own -- the Exhaust hover tip (SecondWind.cs:19) refers to the cards it exhausts -- and the sim leaves `exhausts` False.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new BlockVar(5m, ValueProp.Move)` (SecondWind.cs:17) == `_block = 5`, gained ONCE PER exhausted card. Move without Unpowered -> POWERED block, so NOT in gap G1's blast radius.

OnPlay.rationale: `foreach (item in GetCards().ToList()) { await CardCmd.Exhaust(...); await CreatureCmd.GainBlock(...); }` (SecondWind.cs:29-33), where `GetCards()` is the hand's non-Attacks (41-45), == the sim's `non_attacks = [c for c in ctx.player.hand if c.card_type != CardType.ATTACK]` then per card `ExhaustCmd.exhaust` FOLLOWED BY `BlockCmd.apply`. Three details all match: the candidate list is materialised before the loop (C#'s `.ToList()`, the sim's list comprehension) so mutating the hand mid-loop is safe; the exhaust comes BEFORE its block gain, so a Feel No Pain / Dark Embrace trigger interleaves the same way; and the block is a SEPARATE gain per card rather than one summed gain, which is why creature_card_cmds gap G2 names Second Wind as a witness for Vambrace's per-play latch. Second Wind cannot exhaust itself on either side (Play pile in C#, discard-pile limbo in the sim). Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (28).
